messages:
jamie: quick heads-up — hit a funny edge when validating tenant-scoped API keys behind the proxy. seems like we accept both project_id in the token claim and a forwarded x-project header, but we only enforce one.

devon: ugh that sounds like a TOCTOU. do you have a repro?

jamie: yep. flow: client holds a project-scoped api key (claim: proj=alpha). request goes to edge-proxy which sets x-project=alpha for routing, then calls internal auth service which reads the token and returns actor=service/foo with allowed_projects=[alpha]. but if the proxy is misconfigured it can override x-project to beta and routing will take it, even though token claim is alpha.

miriam: that's bad — basically we trust the header more than the token. what does the authz layer actually check today?

jamie: today most services call authn service with both the token and forwarded project header. authn responds with an actor blob and an "effective_project" picked by authn: currently it prefers header if present.

devon: why prefer header? I thought header was just routing hint. legacy reason: early multi-tenant rollout wanted proxy-driven tenancy for legacy clients.

miriam: ok we need a clear invariant: either token is authoritative or header is subordinate and must be validated against token claims. mixing leads to spoof.

jamie: proposal: change authn service to compute effective_project = intersection(token.allowed_projects, header) if header present; if empty -> reject. if header absent -> pick token primary. Also emit audit fields: claim_project, header_project, effective_project.

devon: +1 for intersection. but consider the migration: some customers rely on proxy override for cross-project proxies (shared infra). how do we avoid breaking them?

jamie: migration plan idea: 1) start in permissive mode where authn logs mismatches but still accepts (with new audit tags). 2) after 2 weeks of no regressions, flip to strict (reject). 3) publish fixups for proxies in infra playbook.

miriam: also add a feature flag per org so we can opt-in early. big enterprise customers may need longer runway.

devon: what about service-to-service tokens and delegated claims? e.g., svc-token minted with project=alpha but services downstream want to act on behalf of client and set header for tenant routing. intersection would still work if token includes delegation scope. we should add a claim: delegated_projects = [] and allow header if header subset of delegated_projects.

jamie: good call. new claim shape: {primary: "alpha", allowed_projects: ["alpha"], delegated_projects: ["beta"]}. rules: header allowed if in allowed_projects OR delegated_projects depending on delegation flag.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: run canary authn with permissive auditing -> 4401234600, add telemetry dashboard -> authn.header-mismatch, notify infra-team.

miriam: perms question: who can mint delegated_projects? only auth-service and token-broker should, not arbitrary services. ensure mint endpoint requires svc_role=broker.

devon: also need to update SDKs and the envoy filter to stop silently overriding headers unless explicitly allowed. add a 1-line config: "preserve_project_header": false by default.

jamie: I'll open a small RFC PR with these rule changes + migration steps. will include snippets:
```
// authn effective project pseudocode
if header.present:
  if header in token.allowed_projects: effective=header
  else if header in token.delegated_projects: effective=header /* allowed via delegation */
  else: if permissive_mode -> effective=token.primary else reject
else:
  effective=token.primary
```

miriam: perfect. add audit log fields and a dashboard query for mismatches by org.

devon: thanks. ping me on the RFC, happy to co-author the migration notes. :thumbsup:

jamie: thanks — filing now. will link the PR here when ready.
